sentences.text: The holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on — has been preserved only as impressions rather than solid bone.
Zhou Zhonghe discovered this fossil in 1994 within the Boluochi quarry of the Jiufotang Formation.
Eocathayornis is a genus of enantiornithean birds, a group considered more basal or primitive than related genera like Sinornis and Cathayornis.
In 2002, Zhou placed Eocathayornis in the family Cathayornithidae.
This extinct avialan lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago in what is now the People's Republic of China.

Recent studies show the phylogenetic position of Eocathayornis is labile, varying between affiliations with Bohaiornithidae, basal positions near Pengornithidae, or advanced positions depending on included taxa. A 2024 analysis supported a clade linking Cathayornis and Eocathayornis, though this was considered less comprehensive than a 2026 study.
